speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To understand the cause of your dizziness, nausea, and imbalance, have you experienced any sudden onset symptoms or head trauma recently? Additionally, are you experiencing hearing changes or ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. The relief from diphenhydramine suggests a vestibular cause; have you noticed any vertigo triggered specifically by rolling over in bed or looking up? Additionally, have you experienced any visual blurring, double vision, or difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The symptoms of sustained spinning and relief with antihistamines are consistent with vestibular pathology, likely triggered by the recent cold, though the constant nature suggests a central component or prolonged peripheral event. I recommend a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm.
